title: Timberwolves @ Pelicans — Arena scoreboard showed wrong score in final minute; Towns fouled thinking Wolves were down 7, not 8 (Dec 31, 2018)
incident_summary: In the final minute of the Pelicans' 123-114 win over the Timberwolves, the in-arena scoreboard displayed an incorrect score that credited Minnesota with an extra point. With about 22 seconds left and the shot clock off, Minnesota was actually down 8 but the board suggested the deficit was 7; Karl-Anthony Towns fouled Julius Randle, who made a free throw to push the lead to 9, and Towns fouled out with about 12 seconds left. The official score was always correct — only the arena display was wrong — but the bad display appears to have changed on-court behavior and the second-half betting result (Timberwolves +second-half spread did not cover).
period_clock: Q4, final minute (~0:22 remaining at the Towns foul)
scoring_play: No single scoring play — a wrong arena scoreboard total (Minnesota +1 phantom point) during live play.

open_questions: Corroboration of the scoreboard error beyond the single Action Network report (priority: broadcast footage, beat-writer accounts, or arena statement). Until then this case stays single-secondary.
Exact technical cause of the wrong display (operator vs. system) — undocumented.
Whether the display was fixed before the final horn or only noticed afterward — undocumented.
betting_notes: Per Action Network: Timberwolves were -3.5 for the second half (+8.5 adjusted with the halftime score); the late foul/FT sequence meant Minnesota did not cover the second half. This is the project's clearest verified example of a display-only error moving a wagering result without touching the official score.
duration_note: Transient display error observed during the final minute of play; total duration undocumented (Action Network). No post-game correction was needed.
